prompt.context_jp: 当直でもないのに、広瀬裕乃____ひとり残って作業を続けていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 広瀬裕乃____ひとり残って作業を続けていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks Hirose Yuno as the ongoing topic of this scene.

feedback.correct_en: Hirose has already been introduced as the focus of this scene (she's the one working late). は frames her as the known topic the sentence is commenting about.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present her as new information just entering the scene — but she is who the narrative is already following, not a newly-spotted figure.

contrast_examples.jp: 広瀬は今日も残業している。
contrast_examples.en: Hirose is working overtime again today. (continuing topic)
Oh, Hirose is still here. (newly noticed)

prompt.context_jp: 技師長の小野寺____戻ってきたのは、そんな夜の遅い時刻のことだった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 技師長の小野寺____戻ってきたのは、そんな夜の遅い時刻のことだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for Onodera entering the scene for the first time.

feedback.correct_en: Onodera is being introduced into the scene as a new participant, and the whole clause 「〜が戻ってきた」 is the new information inside a のは…だ cleft. が marks that fresh subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make Onodera the already-known topic, but he hasn't appeared yet in this scene — he's the newcomer being announced.

contrast_examples.jp: ドアが開いて、男が入ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: The door opened and a man came in. (new entrant)

contrast_examples.jp: 小野寺は毎晩遅く戻る。
contrast_examples.en: Onodera comes back late every night. (established topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「私____遅いだけですし 迷惑かけたくないんで」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私____遅いだけですし、迷惑かけたくないんで。
prompt.prompt_en: Hirose is insisting it is specifically she herself (not anyone else) who is slow.

feedback.correct_en: She is identifying herself exclusively as the one at fault — exhaustive-listing が: 'it's I (and no one else) who is slow.' This fits her self-blaming attitude.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私は would just set up a general comment about herself and wouldn't carry the 'only me' nuance she clearly wants here.

contrast_examples.en: I'll be the one to do it. (I, specifically)
As for me, I'll do it. (just stating her position)

prompt.context_jp: 「むしろ あれは あの男____ね 私の天敵なの！」
prompt.prompt_jp: あの男____ね、私の天敵なの！
prompt.prompt_en: An is emphatically contrasting 'that guy' against any romantic prospect.

feedback.correct_en: She's drawing a sharp contrast: far from being someone she likes, that guy is her enemy. Contrastive は sets him apart from the romantic category Chiaki suggested.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present him as new information, but Chiaki already knows who they're talking about. The point is contrast, not identification.

contrast_examples.en: That person is different (from the rest). (contrast)
That person is the culprit. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: 「五十嵐さん____ 私とは違いますから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 五十嵐さん____ 私とは違いますから。
prompt.prompt_en: Hirose is contrasting Igarashi with herself.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence sets Igarashi apart from 'me' — a textbook contrastive は, reinforced by 私とは later in the same line.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would simply identify Igarashi as the subject, losing the point that she is comparing herself against him.

contrast_examples.en: He is different from me. (contrast)
He's the one in my group. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: 右肩の痛み____続くのに、骨には明らかな異常が見当たらない厄介な症例だった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 右肩の痛み____続くのに、骨には明らかな異常が見当たらない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle introducing the symptom being described.

feedback.correct_en: The pain is new information being presented in a subordinate clause (〜のに). In embedded clauses describing a situation, subjects typically take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would try to make 'right-shoulder pain' a topic, but the topic of the sentence is really the case/症例 — the pain is just a described condition inside the のに-clause.

contrast_examples.jp: 雨が降るのに傘がない。
contrast_examples.en: It's raining but I have no umbrella. (subordinate が)
This pain is a nuisance. (topic は)

prompt.context_jp: 「そんなことより 私____ 高校最後の今年こそ みんなで 全国行きたいの！」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私____ 高校最後の今年こそ みんなで 全国行きたいの！
prompt.prompt_en: Sayaka is contrasting her own priority against the recommendation talk.

feedback.correct_en: She brushes aside the recommendation (そんなこと) and shifts to her own stance: 'as for me, what I want is...' は marks that contrastive personal topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私が would sound like she's identifying herself as 'the one' who wants to go — but her point is a personal declaration, not picking herself out of a group.

contrast_examples.en: I personally don't think so. (contrastive stance)
I'll be the one to go. (I, not anyone else)

prompt.context_jp: 「あいつ____ ただ 諦めなかっただけだ」
prompt.prompt_jp: あいつ____ ただ 諦めなかっただけだ。
prompt.prompt_en: Onodera is summing up Igarashi as the topic of praise.

feedback.correct_en: Onodera is making a general character statement about Igarashi — 'as for that guy, he just didn't give up.' Topic は fits this evaluative comment.
feedback.incorrect_en: あいつが would single him out as the one who didn't give up (vs others), which clashes with Onodera's tone of simply explaining Igarashi's quality.

contrast_examples.jp: あいつは真面目な男だ。
contrast_examples.en: He's a serious guy. (describing)
He's the one who did it. (identifying)

prompt.context_jp: 「間違いないですね これ____ 気胸です」
prompt.prompt_jp: これ____ 気胸です。
prompt.prompt_en: An is identifying the condition shown on the scan she's looking at.

feedback.correct_en: The scan 「これ」 is the shared referent in front of them; she's labeling what it is. 「XはYです」 is the natural pattern for 'this is Y'.
feedback.incorrect_en: これが気胸です would answer 'which one is pneumothorax?' — but no one asked that; she's naming the condition they're all looking at.

contrast_examples.en: This is pneumothorax. (labeling)
THIS one is pneumothorax. (pointing it out among options)

prompt.context_jp: 「肩の痛みの原因____ 骨や関節ではなく肺にありました」
prompt.prompt_jp: 肩の痛みの原因____ 骨や関節ではなく肺にありました。
prompt.prompt_en: An explains where the cause of the shoulder pain actually was.

feedback.correct_en: The patient already knows the question 'what's causing my shoulder pain?' — so 'the cause' is established and takes topic は, with the lung as the new punch line.
feedback.incorrect_en: 原因が would introduce the cause as a fresh subject, but the cause of the pain is exactly what they've been discussing all along — it's the known topic, not new info.

contrast_examples.jp: 痛みの原因は肺でした。
contrast_examples.en: The cause of the pain was the lung. (answering an existing question)

contrast_examples.jp: 新しい原因が見つかった。
contrast_examples.en: A new cause was found. (introducing something new)

prompt.context_jp: 広瀬____また一人で山積みの雑務をこなそうとしており、その姿を先輩たちが遠巻きに眺めている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 広瀬____また一人で山積みの雑務をこなそうとしていた。
prompt.prompt_en: The narration continues to follow Hirose as its focus.

feedback.correct_en: Hirose is the established protagonist the narrator keeps returning to. は signals 'back to Hirose: here's what she was doing.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 広瀬が would announce her as a newly spotted figure, but the chapter has been tracking her all along.

contrast_examples.jp: 広瀬はまた残業していた。
contrast_examples.en: Hirose was once again working late. (continuing topic)
Hirose appeared on the scene. (new entrance)

prompt.context_jp: 「私 バンド____やってるんですけど 初めて人前で演奏した曲なんです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 私 バンド____やってるんですけど。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking what she does.

feedback.correct_en: やる takes a direct object: バンドをやる = 'do/play in a band'. を marks that object.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make the band the subject (as if the band is doing something). で would mean 'at/with a band' as a location/means, which doesn't fit here.

contrast_examples.jp: バンドをやっています。
contrast_examples.en: I'm in a band. (doing the activity)

contrast_examples.jp: バンドで歌っています。
contrast_examples.en: I sing in a band. (band = setting)

prompt.context_jp: 院内で権力を握る鏑木事務長____、自分が他の人より偉いと思う様子を隠さない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 鏑木事務長____、自分が他の人より偉いと思う様子を隠さなかった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames Kaburaki as the subject being described.

feedback.correct_en: This is a general descriptive statement about Kaburaki's character ('as for him, he doesn't hide...'). Topic は fits broad character description.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would read as reporting a one-off action by a newly-introduced person, but the sentence is a general portrait of who he is.

contrast_examples.en: The chief is a strict person. (character description)
The chief shouted. (one event)

prompt.context_jp: 甘春杏____グラスを片手に深いため息をつき、向かいには気心の知れた友人・千秋が座っていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 甘春杏____グラスを片手に深いため息をついた。
prompt.prompt_en: The scene shifts to the izakaya; An becomes the focus.

feedback.correct_en: An is a known main character — the narrator is setting her as the topic for the new scene. は establishes 'as for An, here's what she's doing.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 甘春杏が would present her as a newly discovered subject, but readers already know her from earlier scenes.

contrast_examples.en: An sighed. (continuing / topic frame)

contrast_examples.jp: 一人の女性がため息をついた。
contrast_examples.en: A woman sighed. (new, unidentified subject)

prompt.context_jp: 「あっ もしかして 昨日 私 お水 頂きましたか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 昨日 私 あなた____お水 頂きましたか？
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the source person from whom An received water.

feedback.correct_en: もらう/頂く takes に (or から) to mark the giver — 'received water FROM you'.
feedback.incorrect_en: で marks location/means, not a source person. を would mark the thing received, but 水 already fills that slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 先生に本を頂きました。
contrast_examples.en: I received a book from the teacher.
I bought a book at the store. (location で)

prompt.context_jp: 「真逆なことしてっからな 広瀬と五十嵐____」
prompt.prompt_jp: 広瀬と五十嵐____、真逆なことしてるからな。
prompt.prompt_en: A senior is commenting on Hirose and Igarashi as a pair under discussion.

feedback.correct_en: The two of them have just been raised as a topic ('why is she mad?'). は frames 'those two' as what the comment is about.
feedback.incorrect_en: 広瀬と五十嵐が真逆なことしている would state it as newly observed news, but the senior is explaining the known pair's dynamic.

contrast_examples.jp: あの二人は性格が真逆だ。
contrast_examples.en: Those two are opposite in personality. (describing a known pair)

contrast_examples.jp: 二人が同時に走り出した。
contrast_examples.en: The two of them started running at the same time. (event report)

prompt.context_jp: 「何 ____してんだよ お前 明日やれることは 明日やる」
prompt.prompt_jp: 何 ____してんだよ、お前。
prompt.prompt_en: Onodera is telling Hirose to stop holding back and ask for help.

feedback.correct_en: 遠慮する = 'hold back / be reserved out of consideration' — exactly what Hirose does by not asking colleagues for help. 「何遠慮してんだよ」 = 'Why are you holding back?'
feedback.incorrect_en: 心配 (worry) and 我慢 (endure) don't fit — he isn't scolding her for worrying or enduring pain, but for being overly reserved.

contrast_examples.jp: 遠慮しないで食べてね。
contrast_examples.en: Don't hold back, eat up.

contrast_examples.jp: 我慢しないで言ってね。
contrast_examples.en: Don't bottle it up — tell me. (enduring pain/feelings)

prompt.context_jp: 「____は禁物ですよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: ____は禁物ですよ。
prompt.prompt_en: The doctor tells the patient not to rush her recovery.

feedback.correct_en: 焦りは禁物 is a set phrase meaning 'rushing is forbidden / don't be impatient' — a stock line a doctor would use when a patient wants a quick fix.
feedback.incorrect_en: 怒り (anger) and 疲れ (fatigue) don't form the idiom. The context is specifically about her impatience to be healed quickly.

contrast_examples.en: You mustn't rush things.
Don't let your guard down. (same pattern, different noun)

prompt.context_jp: 「もし そうであったならば ____を争う状況です」
prompt.prompt_jp: ____を争う状況です。
prompt.prompt_en: Igarashi stresses how urgent the suspected diagnosis would be.

feedback.correct_en: 一刻を争う is a set phrase meaning 'every moment counts / a race against time' — exactly what femoral head necrosis would require.
feedback.incorrect_en: 勝負を争う and 時間を争う aren't standard idioms; medical urgency in Japanese is conventionally expressed as 一刻を争う.

contrast_examples.en: It's a surgery where every second counts.
It's a race against time. (different idiom)

prompt.context_jp: 「それにしても この写真 関節の____が甘いな」
prompt.prompt_jp: この写真、関節の____が甘いな。
prompt.prompt_en: Onodera critiques the X-ray's clarity on the joint area.

feedback.correct_en: In radiology jargon, 抜け refers to the clarity/sharpness of the gap between joints on an X-ray. 「抜けが甘い」 = 'the sharpness isn't quite there'.
feedback.incorrect_en: 写り (how something is captured) and 影 (shadow) are related photo terms but aren't the technical word for joint-space resolution in Japanese radiology.

contrast_examples.en: The joint space isn't sharp enough. (radiology)
The photo didn't come out well. (general)

prompt.context_jp: 「機転を____せて 広めに撮影したのは 間違いなく 広瀬さんのファインプレーです」
prompt.prompt_jp: 機転を____せて広めに撮影した。
prompt.prompt_en: An praises Hirose for her quick thinking.

feedback.correct_en: 機転を利かせる is the standard idiom meaning 'use one's wits / show quick thinking'. 利かせる (making 機転 work) is the fixed form.
feedback.incorrect_en: 機転を合わせる and 機転を寄せる are not idiomatic combinations; only 利かせる collocates with 機転.

contrast_examples.jp: 機転を利かせて切り抜ける。
contrast_examples.en: Get through it with quick thinking.

contrast_examples.jp: 気を利かせてお茶を出す。
contrast_examples.en: Thoughtfully serve some tea. (similar pattern with 気)

prompt.context_jp: 「気胸による胸の痛みは 肩に____することもあり 肩の痛みだと感じる人もいます」
prompt.prompt_jp: 胸の痛みは肩に____することもある。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb describing how pain spreads from the chest to the shoulder.

feedback.correct_en: 拡散 = spread/diffuse — the correct medical description of referred pain radiating from one area to another (痛みが肩に拡散する).
feedback.incorrect_en: 分散 = disperse/distribute (as in splitting a load); 発散 = give off/release (energy, stress). Neither fits pain radiating in the body.

contrast_examples.en: The pain radiates to the shoulder.
Release stress. (different nuance)

prompt.context_jp: すっぽん 500匹分のエキスを配合した 最強の____ドリンク
prompt.prompt_jp: 最強の____ドリンク
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that describes a health/energy drink.

feedback.correct_en: 滋養強壮ドリンク is the fixed category label for traditional 'tonic/stamina' drinks (think Lipovitan). This is what Omori keeps on her shelf.
feedback.incorrect_en: 栄養補給 (nutritional supplement) and 疲労回復 (fatigue recovery) describe effects, but the standard product-category name is 滋養強壮(ドリンク/剤).

contrast_examples.jp: 滋養強壮ドリンクを飲む。
contrast_examples.en: Drink a tonic drink. (product category)
Replenish nutrients. (describes an action)

prompt.context_jp: 「この程度の知識のない者を カンファレンスに参加させないで いただけますか 人員の____ですから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 人員の____ですから。
prompt.prompt_en: The doctor rudely says bringing an unqualified person is a waste of staffing.

feedback.correct_en: 人員の無駄 = 'a waste of personnel' — bitter workplace jab that unqualified staff being present wastes a seat.
feedback.incorrect_en: 不足 (shortage) and 過剰 (surplus) would mean the opposite — he's not complaining about numbers but about wasting a slot.

contrast_examples.en: It's a waste of time.
We're short on staff. (opposite complaint)

prompt.context_jp: 「俺たちなら いくら 迷惑かけても チームなんだからよ なっ？ もう ____すんなよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: もう____すんなよ。
prompt.prompt_en: Onodera tells Hirose to stop holding back from the team.

feedback.correct_en: This echoes Onodera's earlier 「何遠慮してんだよ」. His whole message is: we're a team, stop being so reserved about asking for help.
feedback.incorrect_en: 緊張 (nervousness) and 後悔 (regret) don't match — the issue isn't nerves or past regret, but her habit of pulling back from the group.

contrast_examples.jp: 遠慮なく頼ってください。
contrast_examples.en: Rely on us without reserve.
Don't be nervous. (different situation)

prompt.context_jp: Hirose insists she's nothing like Igarashi.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural for Hirose comparing herself to Igarashi?

choices.text: 五十嵐さんは 私とは違いますから
五十嵐さんが 私と違いますから
五十嵐さんは 私と違いますが

feedback.correct_en: The double は (五十嵐さんは…私とは) creates the contrastive 'he, as opposed to me' pairing that Hirose intends.
feedback.incorrect_en: Option b uses が, flattening the contrast into mere identification. Option c drops the contrastive は on 私, making the comparison weaker, and ends with が which leaves the thought dangling.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼は私とは違う世界の人だ。
contrast_examples.en: He's from a different world than I am. (dual contrast)
He's the one in a different group from me. (identification)

prompt.context_jp: An stops Igarashi in the hallway to thank him properly.
prompt.prompt_en: Which thank-you fits An's awkward-but-polite moment best?

choices.text: 色々と ありがとうございました
いろいろ ありがとね
本日は誠に感謝申し上げます

feedback.correct_en: 色々とありがとうございました is a warm but polite thank-you — appropriate for a colleague she's not quite close with, and it matches the slightly stiff mood of this scene.
feedback.incorrect_en: b (ありがとね) is too casual for the strained working relationship. c (誠に感謝申し上げます) is business-formal boilerplate — much too stiff for a personal moment between coworkers.

contrast_examples.jp: 色々とありがとうございました。
contrast_examples.en: Thank you for everything. (polite, personal)

contrast_examples.jp: 誠に感謝申し上げます。
contrast_examples.en: I express my sincere gratitude. (formal, impersonal)

prompt.context_jp: An announces her diagnosis after reading the new scan.
prompt.prompt_en: Which line sounds most natural as a confident diagnosis announcement?

choices.text: 間違いないですね。これは気胸です
間違いないですね。これが気胸です
間違いないですね。これは気胸がです

feedback.correct_en: これは気胸です is the natural 'X is Y' labeling for what everyone is already looking at. It matches a doctor confidently naming the condition.
feedback.incorrect_en: b (これが) would answer 'which one is pneumothorax?' — wrong discourse context. c is ungrammatical (は and が can't stack like that).

contrast_examples.en: This is a fracture. (labeling what's on the scan)

contrast_examples.jp: これが問題の部分です。
contrast_examples.en: THIS is the problem area. (pointing out among others)

prompt.context_jp: Hirose apologizes to Onodera for still being at work.
prompt.prompt_en: Which apology best matches Hirose's junior-to-boss tone?

choices.text: すいません、作業終わらなくて
ごめん、まだ仕事が残ってて
申し訳ございません、業務が完了しておりませんので

feedback.correct_en: すいません + plain -て apology is standard mid-politeness speech between a junior tech and her chief — polite but conversational, which is exactly what the drama uses.
feedback.incorrect_en: b (ごめん) is too casual for a boss. c (申し訳ございません…おりません) is customer-service-level formal — out of place in a late-night internal conversation.

contrast_examples.jp: すいません、遅れました。
contrast_examples.en: Sorry, I'm late. (workplace casual-polite)

contrast_examples.jp: 申し訳ございません、遅れております。
contrast_examples.en: We sincerely apologize, we are running late. (customer-facing formal)

prompt.context_jp: An insists Igarashi is her 'natural enemy', not a love interest.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version best captures An's contrastive emphasis?

choices.text: むしろ あの男はね、私の天敵なの！
むしろ あの男がね、私の天敵なの！
むしろ あの男を、私の天敵なの！

feedback.correct_en: After むしろ ('on the contrary'), 「あの男は」 sets up a contrastive topic — he is, far from a crush, the opposite. The ね softens it into expressive speech.
feedback.incorrect_en: b uses が which would identify him as the enemy (as if picking among options). c uses を but 天敵 is a predicate noun, not a direct object — it's ungrammatical.

contrast_examples.en: That person is, if anything, an enemy. (contrastive)
That person is the ally. (identification)
